basis: The complete final paragraph of XVIII.31 explicitly interprets the written vision, appointed end, waiting and certain coming as the advent of Christ. The witness's note 533 and the actual held canonical verses agree on Habakkuk 2:2-3. The preceding Obadiah and Nahum units and the chapter's initial dating discussion are outside this naturally separate paragraph, and are not silently joined to it.
date_basis: The retained Dods 1871 volume I introduction, artifact.augustine.de-civitate-dei.dods-1871.pg45304-body-lf lines 239-243, dates composition of the work from 413 to 426. This ordering key uses the first year of that stated range, as the accepted existing City of God rows do; it does not establish the exact year of this book, chapter or paragraph. The work record has no composed field, and no existing source fingerprint or reviewed binding is changed.
text: Of what else than the advent of Christ, who was to come, is Habakkuk understood to say, "And the Lord answered me, and said, Write the vision openly on a tablet of boxwood, that he that readeth these things may understand. For the vision is yet for a time appointed, and it will arise in the end, and will not become void: if it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, and will not be delayed?"
